svg.title: 204 · Placental arrows must agree with the row
svg.desc: Answer B: tissue P represents maternal blood and substance 2 is urea. A qualitative exchange model retains the original left-to-right order P, placenta, Q. With P maternal and Q fetal, arrow 1 points right from P to Q, the direction for nutrient supply such as amino acids. Arrow 2 points left from Q to P, the direction for fetal wastes such as urea and carbon dioxide. The source identifies only substance 2 as urea in the correct row; arrow 1 is not uniquely named. The option checks explain why carbon dioxide cannot be arrow 1 with P maternal, and why amino acids cannot be arrow 1 with Q maternal. Starch is not transported across the placenta as starch. No blood mixing, concentrations or measured transport rates are depicted.

g.text: 204 · Placental arrows must agree with the row
Check the tissue identity and the substance together.
Tissue P
Maternal blood
Tissue Q
Fetal blood
Placenta
Substance 1 →
← Substance 2
Same P → Q and Q → P directions as the source.
Mother → fetus
Nutrients such as amino acids travel this way.
Arrow 1 could represent a supplied nutrient.
Fetus → mother
Waste products such as urea travel this way.
Arrow 2 = urea makes row B consistent.
A: carbon dioxide would move the other way.
C: if Q were maternal, arrow 1 would be wrong for amino acids.
D: starch is not transported across the placenta as starch.
Qualitative exchange model; no blood mixing or rates are shown.
Answer B · P is maternal blood · Substance 2 is urea
